task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Brush/Roll)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Drop cloth placement per frame location. ~4 min per frame. Simpler setup than door slab (no door swing).

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Spray)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Rosin paper 8ft radius per frame opening. ~7-8 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Adjacent Protection (Spray)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask wall adjacent to frame opening. ~6 min per frame (both sides of opening).
task_production_rates.state_condition_note: Task inclusion based on adjacent wall state driven by state_declarations.adjacent_state_protection_rules for wall_field.

task_production_rates.name: Mask Door Hardware (Hinges + Strike Plate)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask 3 hinge leaves + strike plate. ~6 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Frame Surface
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection per frame set (3 jambs + stop). QT2: Quick glance at 8-10 ft ~1 min (upper range ~40/hr). QT3: Note obvious defects ~2 min. QT4: Systematic at 3 ft ~3 min. QT5: Critical with light ~4 min. Faster than door slab (simpler geometry).

task_production_rates.name: Sand Frame Surface (Prep)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Scuff sand all jamb and stop surfaces. QT2: Light scuff 180 grit quick pass ~4 min (upper range ~15/hr). QT3: Uniform scratch pattern ~5 min. QT4+: Thorough ~6-7 min. Less surface area than door slab.

task_production_rates.name: Fill Stop Nail Holes
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fill nail holes in door stop. ~6-8 holes per frame typical. QT2: Obvious/large holes only ~2 min (upper range ~25/hr). QT3: Obvious holes ~3 min. QT4: All visible ~4 min. QT5: Every hole ~5 min.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Filled Areas
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand filler spots smooth. ~2 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Frame-to-Casing Gap
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Caulk gap between frame and casing. ~6 min per frame (both sides of jambs + head).

task_production_rates.name: Clean Sanding Dust
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe all frame surfaces. ~1.5 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Primer on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray primer coat on frame set. ~4 min per frame. Faster than slab (simpler geometry).

task_production_rates.name: Brush Primer on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush primer coat on frame set. ~7-8 min per frame. Brush is ~1.2x spray time.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Coat (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection between coats. QT2: Quick glance for failures only ~1 min (upper range ~40/hr). QT3: Quick ~1.5 min. QT4: Systematic ~2.5 min. QT5: Critical ~3.5 min.

task_production_rates.name: Light Sand Between Coats
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: QT2: Quick scuff 180 single pass ~1.5 min (upper range ~15/hr), ~20% faster than QT3. QT3: Spot sand ~2 min. QT4: Full sand 220 ~5 min. QT5: Thorough 320 ~6 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot patch defects found during interstage inspection. QT2: Skip unless coating failure risk ~0.5 min (upper range). QT3: Glaring defects ~2 min. QT4: All marked ~3 min. QT5: All defects ~4 min. QT2 saves ~5-10 min per frame on interstage repair.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe between coats. ~1.5 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat on frame set. ~5 min per frame. Slightly slower than primer for quality finish.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat on frame set. ~10 min per frame. Work systematically: head → jambs → stop.

task_production_rates.name: Roll and Tip Finish Coat on Frame
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll and Tip method: roller deposits, brush tips. ~8-9 min per frame. Slightly faster than brush-only.

task_production_rates.name: Touch Up Mortise Areas
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch up 3 hinge mortises + 1 strike mortise per frame. ~4 min per frame. Bundled per-frame, not per-hinge.

task_production_rates.name: Final Frame Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final inspection per frame. QT2: Quick glance at 8-10 ft, obvious failures only ~1 min (upper range ~40/hr). QT3: 6 ft ~1.5 min. QT4: 3 ft ~2.5 min. QT5: Arm's length ~3.5 min. Minor brush marks/orange peel acceptable at QT2.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Hardware Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove masking tape from hinges and strike plate. ~3 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove floor protection per frame location. ~2.5 min per frame.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove wall masking. ~3 min per frame.
task_production_rates.state_condition_note: Task inclusion based on adjacent wall state driven by state_declarations.adjacent_state_protection_rules for wall_field.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time: ~30-45 min per session regardless of frame count. Modeled as flat allowance.

quality_tier_effects.description: Economy door frame painting — reduced prep, basic coverage
quality_tier_effects.notes: QT2 SCOPE REDUCTION: Quick inspection at 8-10 ft (no marking), light scuff sand only (no targeted repair), fill only obvious holes, skip interstage defect repair unless coating failure risk. IMPORTANT: Application quality (no drips/sags/runs/holidays) is NOT reduced — binary application tasks are identical at all tiers. Sheen NOT limited for trim (semi-gloss standard). Two coats remain standard. QT2 time savings (~20%) come from reduced prep/interstage rigor, not from faster application. Per Modifier_Registry QT2_MINIMAL = 0.8

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard door frame painting — baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard NC production. Per Modifier_Registry QT3_STANDARD = 1.0

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium door frame painting — thorough prep, full sand between coats
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Modifier_Registry QT4_PREMIUM = 1.30. Per research.json notes: QT4=1.30.

quality_tier_effects.description: Superior door frame painting — maximum care, zero tolerance
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Modifier_Registry QT5_SUPERIOR = 1.50. Per research.json notes: QT5=1.50.

frame_type_complexity.notes: Standard swing door frame. Full jambs + stop. Baseline.
Pocket door frame. No door stop (door slides into wall). ~15% less surface area.
Cased opening (no door). Jambs only, no stop, no hardware. ~25% less work.
Bifold door frame. Track hardware instead of hinges. No mortise touch-up. ~10% less work.

height_access_effects.notes: Floor-level access. Baseline. Per Modifier_Registry H1_STANDARD = 1.0
Step/extension ladder for head jamb. Per Modifier_Registry H2_TALL = 1.30
Scaffold likely required. Rare for door frames. Per Modifier_Registry H3_HIGH = 1.50

application_method_effects.notes: Fastest production method. Baseline for coating application tasks.
Per research.json: brush/roll typically 1.15-1.25x spray time. Using 1.20 as midpoint.
Faster than brush-only, slower than spray. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine § 15.6.

crew_configurations.name: Single Frame Sprayer
crew_configurations.notes: One sprayer handles all frames. Helper for masking/protection setup.

crew_configurations.name: Single Frame Brush Painter
crew_configurations.notes: One painter brushes frames. Can use Roll and Tip for larger jamb surfaces.

rate_comparison_notes.frame_vs_slab: Door frames are FASTER than door slabs. Simpler geometry (no panels, no complex edges). Expect frame rates to be ~1.5x faster than equivalent slab tasks.
rate_comparison_notes.pca_measurement_note: Per PCA standards, surfaces <1 ft width are measured as 1 LF regardless of actual width. No frame width modifier applies. A 4-inch frame and 6-inch frame are equivalent from a production perspective.

assumptions.value: Frame tasks ~1.5x faster than equivalent slab tasks
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines frame vs slab rate ratios. Derived from geometry analysis.

assumptions.value: Mortise touch-up bundled per-frame, not per-hinge
assumptions.note: Practical estimation bundles as single task per frame.
